messages:
maria: quick follow-up to the RFC — we still need to decide where the 'telemetry sanitizer' shim lives. do we put it at the edge gateway, in the ingest pipeline, or as a sidecar next to runtime?
kevin: prefer edge gateway for early PII-drop but worried about duplicating routing logic 
alex: +1 on edge for PII, but the gateway has limited context for some model-level metadata we want to preserve (model_version, rollout_tag)
jun: architecture tradeoff: early drop reduces storage/TOS exposure but makes rollback harder if we realize we dropped useful fields. ingest-level gives full context and easier reprocessing if needed.
maria: good point. ingest also lets us run richer heuristics (regexes + ML classifiers) before scrubbing. but ingest increases TTF and storage of raw logs until scrubbed.
kevin: performance numbers? any rough latency/Throughput estimates if we add a sanitizer step in ingest?
alex: did a rough local test: single-threaded sanitizer (regex + simple named-entity model) adds ~3ms per event; scaled/pipelined it becomes <0.5ms average with batching. cost is extra CPU fleet.
maria: so edge adds ~0.5ms, ingest adds ~0.5ms but more ops and reprocessing flexibility. sidecar gives per-customer opt-in per deployment, but operational surface triples.
jun: another dimension: observability. We need telemetry that lets us detect 'sanitizer regressions' (e.g., too aggressive redaction). idea: emit sanitizer-delta signals (hashes of fields removed, sanitized_field_count) but those are themselves sensitive.
kevin: propose a compact telemetry contract: emit counts by safe buckets (email_removed: 1, phone_removed: 0) and a signature for sampling. no raw values.
maria: agreed. also we should add a 'dry-run' mode where sanitizer annotates events instead of dropping fields so downstream evals can run. rollout plan: 1) edge dry-run for 10% tenants, 2) ingest dry-run for 100% but keep raw in quarantine for 7 days, 3) enable drop for low-risk tenants, 4) full drop after audit.
alex: implementation note: keep sanitizer logic versioned and immutable (sanitizer_v1, v2) so we can backfill or replay using the same transformation. store version in event metadata.
jun: +1 on versioning. also need migration signal for customers: an opt-out header X-RW-sanitize=off for enterprise tenants during testing. must be logged and gated by an admin flag.
kevin: privacy/legal flagged the quarantine idea as OK if retention is short and access controlled. they insisted on audit logs for any raw access.
maria: tests: we need a composable test harness with prompt/trace fixtures. example fixture: user prompt with contact info + code snippet. assert sanitized output patterns and metrics. include fuzz tests for different languages and tokenization edge cases.
alex: ops: deploy-bot will emit canary deploy + telemetry summary: `deploy-bot: sanitizer-canary deployed v1 -> 10% tenants, avg sanitize_ms=0.6, removed_fields=email:23, phone:5`
deploy-bot: sanitizer-canary deployed v1 -> 10% tenants, avg_sanitize_ms=0.6, removed_fields=email:23,phone:5
maria: final decision proposal: implement sanitizer as a hybrid — primary in ingest (for replayability + richer heuristics) with an optional edge prefilter (cheap regexes) to drop obviously risky tokens earlier. telemetry contract = aggregated buckets + sanitizer_version. rollout as described. objections?
jun: sounds good. only ask: add a kill-switch that can flip to dry-run and a way to snapshot the quarantine store for legal holds.
kevin: add item to run a small benchmark on p95 latency impact across typical request mix. I'll take that.
maria: i'll update the RFC with these ops/telemetry/runbook items and add the rollout windows. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
alex: thanks — i'll draft the sanitizer proto and unit tests, pinging @kevin for perf numbers.
kevin: will post perf numbers by EOD tomorrow.
maria: closing notes: keep telemetry minimal, version everything, provide dry-run & opt-out for tenants, quarantine raw for 7 days, audit logs for access. we'll reconvene after perf numbers. :eyes:
